Split out of chewed-illicit-blacklemur (b8f7-65be-ec00-4844). Distinct defect, distinct fix.

TEST: tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py::test_plan_review_sidecar_emit_two_clone_union
(and its two siblings, test_code_review_* / test_completion_*, which share the same helper).

SIGNATURE: AssertionError: clones do not share a base

## Confirmed root cause

The failing assertion is a FIXTURE PRECONDITION, not the I1 append-only invariant under test.
In `_assert_emit_is_append_only`, clone A pushes its padded sidecar base to origin/tickets and
clone B is then expected to hold the same base. B's sync is driven only as an incidental side
effect of a read:

    _git("push", "-q", "origin", "HEAD:tickets", cwd=tracker_a)
    _expire_sync_marker(tracker_b)
    _engine_run(repo_b, "list")          # <- the only thing that syncs B
    ...
    assert base_a == _sidecar_paths(tracker_b, ...), "clones do not share a base"

That read-freshness path is best-effort BY DESIGN. `rebar._engine_support.reads.ensure_fresh`
is throttled by a /tmp marker, calls `reconverge` with a deliberately SHORT lock timeout, and
swallows every failure ("a read must never fail because a fetch could not run"). So `list`
returns 0 whether or not B pulled A's push. Under CI load (contended lock / slow runner) the
reconverge is skipped or times out silently, B keeps its stale base, and the test fails while
building its own setup. The append-only behaviour the test exists to prove is never reached,
so the red is a false alarm that costs a Verified -1.

Reproduced deterministically on this checkout by forcing the incidental sync to be a no-op
(`REBAR_SYNC_PULL=off`, which `ensure_fresh` honours): all three two-clone-union tests fail
with exactly `AssertionError: clones do not share a base`. With the sync left enabled they
pass. That isolates the precondition to the best-effort side effect and rules out a product
defect in sidecar emit.

## Fix

Make the fixture ASSERT its precondition instead of relying on a side effect:

1. Add a `_sync_from_origin(tracker)` helper that fetches `origin tickets` and fast-forwards
   the tracker onto `FETCH_HEAD`, both with `check=True`, so a sync failure raises at its own
   call site as a setup error rather than surfacing later as a misleading invariant failure.
2. Replace `_expire_sync_marker(tracker_b)` + `_engine_run(repo_b, "list")` in
   `_assert_emit_is_append_only` with that explicit call.
3. Label the two setup assertions distinctly from the I1 invariant assertions so triage can
   tell a setup failure from a real append-only violation.
4. Document at the helper why the production read path must NOT be used to establish a
   fixture precondition.

Deterministic sync, not a retry loop. Content/ordering assertions only - no wall-clock or
timing-budget assertions are added.

Scope: tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py only. No production code changes; the
product behaviour under test is unchanged and still fully exercised.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: `_assert_emit_is_append_only` establishes clone B's shared base with an explicit
      checked `git fetch` + `git merge --ff-only`; it no longer calls `_engine_run(repo_b,
      "list")` or `_expire_sync_marker` to make the base converge.
- [ ] AC2: The two shared-base preconditions are asserted with messages that identify them as
      SETUP failures, textually distinct from the I1 append-only invariant messages.
- [ ] AC3: With the incidental read-sync disabled (`REBAR_SYNC_PULL=off`) all three
      `*_sidecar_emit_two_clone_union` tests PASS on the fixed code; on the pre-fix code the
      same command fails all three with `AssertionError: clones do not share a base`.
- [ ] AC4: All three tests pass under the default environment, and the file adds no wall-clock
      or timing-budget assertion (assertions remain content/ordering facts).
- [ ] AC5: `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
